rule: Protect architectural principles, not inherited dimensions. Unknown project-specific temporary-work requirements must not become canonical geometry by guesswork.

PROTECTED.property: A real internal courtyard remains a primary spatial/environmental object rather than a decorative lightwell.
No service inside permanent fabric; service zones/cavities remain accessible and replaceable.
Maintenance access remains designed and comprehensible without turning the house into an exposed technical object.
Wet/service functions remain deliberately clustered so infrastructure is short, legible and maintainable.
Principal rooms retain generous usable proportions, ceiling quality and calm; compactness may not be purchased by mean rooms.
The principal stair remains an architectural room/circulation object with deep-tread quality and credible clearances.
The house retains a legible front-to-rear domestic hierarchy and a strong relationship to the rear garden.
The outward house remains classically/Georgian composed rather than becoming arbitrary contemporary massing to solve the plot.
Major maintainable/replaced elements, including courtyard-facing elements, must have an explicit credible replacement route.
Water management, movement interfaces and maintainability continue to prefer geometry and designed interfaces over sealant/chemistry dependence.

HIGH_RESISTANCE.property: The courtyard should remain spatially central enough to organise the house; meaningful offset is allowed only where the resulting plan is better, not merely narrower.
The present two-storey domestic order is the default. Extra storeys/basement are not a cheap way to recover footprint.
The house should retain distinct principal domestic territories rather than solving width entirely through one undifferentiated open plan.
Both detached side elevations should remain inspectable and ordinarily reachable. One side may carry more technical duty, but the other should not become a meaningless leftover slot.
Front elevation hierarchy and bay rhythm should remain capable of a calm classical composition; internal optimisation may not leave the facade as an afterthought.

FLEXIBLE: number and position of secondary side windows
bay widths and exact facade opening centres
door positions and local circulation geometry
external plant location where serviceability and quietness survive
PROJECT_SPECIFIC: exact ASHP or other plant model clearances
neighbour window positions and privacy rights

successorGenerationRules: Do not uniformly scale the B4 plan.
Do not choose a target shell width before spatial concepts are compared.
Include the current B4 arrangement as a control where useful.
Every candidate must show ground and first floors together on RSI-RS-01.
Every candidate must state what it gains in side territory and what architectural cost pays for it.
Every candidate must expose service/wet-room geography and a courtyard replacement route.
Every candidate must be checked on the 14 x 40 m counterfactual without separate optimisation.
No candidate may rely on project-specific temporary-work dimensions invented for RSI.
No candidate may become canonical before OWNER GATE A and OWNER GATE B.
ownerGateAReadyWhen: 3-5 materially different rough plan concepts exist
all schemes preserve protected principles or explicitly flag a proposed freeze break
trade-offs are visible without PLT styling
current B4 control is available for comparison
plot and side-territory consequences are shown
